style_conflict_warning.issue: All five finished reference panels use a dark CHARCOAL GRADIENT banner with ALL-CAPS white type. The 8.17.26 Staples style guide forbids both - 'Don't use gradients' (section 1.3) and 'Capitalize only the very first letter of the sentence or phrase' (section 4.2).
style_conflict_warning.resolution: FOLLOW THE STYLE GUIDE, NOT THE ART. Use a flat Slate #262020 fill where the reference uses a gradient, and sentence case where the reference uses caps. The generated output will deliberately NOT match the reference on these two points.
style_conflict_warning.why_this_is_a_feature: It is worth showing Sandeep directly. A pipeline driven by a machine-readable ruleset cannot drift from the brand the way a manual process does. The side-by-side on this SKU makes that argument better than any slide could.
style_conflict_warning.also: Reference panel _2 misspells 'separately' as 'seperately'. Do not reproduce it.

pipeline_mix.note: FIVE generated photographs and not a single flat graphic card. This is the most photography-heavy SKU in the set and therefore the best showcase of nano-banana specifically. It is also the only Staples-brand SKU with a complete plan, so it is what proves the pipeline is not just a Coastwide-orange trick.
pipeline_mix.why_no_graphic_only_shots: The brief's six-shot plan simply doesn't call for one - every slot is product or lifestyle photography. That is a property of this product, not an omission. A pen has no dimensions shot (the guide forbids it), no what's-in-the-box beyond the refills, and no surfaces grid.

demo_recommendation: Run this SKU second, after ExpressMop. ExpressMop proves the full branching pipeline with a complete reference set; ProGel proves it works on a different brand, a different product category, and a photography-only stack - including a human hand, which is the shot most likely to impress and most likely to fail.
